name: cutter-overshoot-floor
source: mcweed heating-core tube: 'What are these huge holes on the bottom of the heating core tube?' A generously oversized groove cutter, centred on the face it entered, punched the grooves clean through the 1.25 mm floor. Nobody looked at the underside until the print.
summary: Six 1 mm deep, 2 mm wide radial grooves in the top face of a 4 mm disc. The trap is the 'always make cutters bigger than the body' reflex: a tall cutter centred on the top face spans the whole thickness and turns the grooves into through slots. Overshoot belongs only where nothing has to survive - radially past the rim and upwards above the top face - with the cutter bottomed at z = discH - depth.
